overview.description: Australian Patience is a strategic solitaire game that blends the layout of Klondike with the move-logic of Scorpion. It is characterized by having all tableau cards face-up from the start, requiring the player to build down in suit. Unlike Klondike, any cards sitting on top of a card being moved are carried along, making it a game of foresight and column management.

history.origins: Originating in Australia as a more skill-based alternative to Klondike. It gained international popularity in the digital era as part of high-difficulty solitaire collections.
timeline: Early 20th Century: Variations of open-layout solitaire emerge in the UK and Commonwealth.
1990s: Inclusion in early computer solitaire packages alongside Scorpion and Yukon.
Present: Recognized as one of the 'top-tier' strategic solitaires due to its low luck factor compared to Klondike.
history.evolution: The game simplifies the 'hidden card' mechanic of Klondike by making everything visible, which shifts the challenge from discovery to optimization.
history.cultural: Favored by competitive solitaire players who enjoy 'solvable' puzzles where defeat is usually the result of a misplay rather than a bad shuffle.

setup.players: One player for the standard solitaire game. The player shuffles and deals their own tableau; there is no dealer or opponent. Australian Patience can also be played competitively by two players (each with their own 52-card pack and tableau), but the primary form documented here is single-player.
setup.dealing: 7 columns of 4 cards are dealt face-up, slightly overlapped. This uses 28 cards. The remaining 24 cards form the draw pile (stock).

rules.objective: Move all 52 cards to the four foundation piles, organized by suit from Ace to King.
rules.gameplay: 1. Deal: 7 columns of 4 cards each, face-up (28 cards). Stock = 24 cards. 2. Play: Build tableau down in suit only. Move cards (and any cards on top) to other columns or to foundations. Flip stock one at a time to waste; top of waste is playable. 3. Foundations: Aces up in suit (A-2-3...K). 4. Win when all 52 cards are on foundations.
keyRules: Suit Building: You MUST follow suit in the tableau (unlike Klondike's alternating colors).
Visibility: All 28 starting cards are visible; use this to plan 3-4 moves ahead.
No Redeal: If the stock is empty and no moves remain, the game is lost.

strategy.basic: Prioritize exposing and moving Aces to the foundations immediately. Without your Aces, you cannot clear any cards.
strategy.intermediate: Column Management: Avoid creating empty columns unless you have a King ready to move into it. An empty column with no King is a wasted space that could have held card sequences.
strategy.advanced: Look-Ahead Analysis: Since all cards are face-up, identify 'Blocks'. For example, if the 5 of Hearts is trapped under the 7 of Hearts, you must find a way to move the 7 before you can ever play that 5.
tips: The 'No Redeal' rule makes every card in the waste pile precious. Don't flip a stock card if you have a viable move on the tableau.
Try to keep your tableau sequences 'pure' (uninterrupted suit order) to make them easier to move later.

list.name: Competitive Australian
list.description: Two players play with their own decks. The first to clear their foundations wins.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Variation describes the two-player competitive format; core engine remains shared with the solitaire version.

difficulty.easy: Builds sequences in alternating colors by mistake (Klondike habit). Flips stock cards immediately without checking the tableau.
difficulty.medium: Understands suit-building. Identifies Aces in the tableau and works to free them.
difficulty.hard: Performs exhaustive search of the state space. Anticipates when a King move will 'unblock' a critical card beneath it. Maintains 100% legal play efficiency.

considerations: AI must treat the game as a 'Perfect Information' puzzle since all initial cards are visible.
Heuristics should prioritize 'Unburying' low-rank foundation cards.

ante.reason: Australian Patience is solitaire with no betting or ante.

deal.reason: Dealing is done via custom setup_7x4 action; no generic deal action.

reveal_market.reason: No market pile; only stock and waste in this solitaire.

buy_market.reason: There is no market or purchase mechanic in this patience game.

buy_stock.reason: Cards are flipped from stock to waste only; no buying from stock.

fold.reason: Single-player solitaire; no fold or surrender action.

check.reason: No betting rounds; check does not apply to this game.

call.reason: No betting; call is not used in Australian Patience.

bet.reason: Patience has no wagering or bet action.

raise.reason: No betting; raise does not apply to this solitaire.

declare.reason: No declaration phase; players build foundations only.

reveal_hand.reason: Tableau cards are always face-up; no reveal-hand phase.

award_pot.reason: No pot or wager pool; win is by clearing all cards to foundations.

play_card.reason: Moves use custom actions move_tableau_group and move_to_foundation.

draw.reason: Drawing is flipping stock to waste via custom flip_stock action.

discard.reason: Waste is a flip target only; no discard-from-hand in this game.

pass.reason: Player always acts on tableau or waste; no pass action.

bid.reason: No bidding; single player builds foundations only.

meld.reason: No melding; cards move to tableau or foundations only.

go_out.reason: Win is verified by system via verify_win when foundations are full.

notApplicableReasons.discardConfig: Waste pile receives cards only from stock flips; there is no discard-from-hand or pick-from-discard mechanic.

customActions.description: Deal 7 columns of 4 cards each face-up to the tableau.
Move a card and any cards on top of it to another tableau column (build down in suit).
customActions.constraints: Destination column top card must be next-higher in same suit.

customActions.description: Move a card to a foundation (A-up in suit).
customActions.constraints: Card must be next in sequence for that foundation.

customActions.description: Flip the top stock card to waste.
Move the top waste card to tableau or foundation.
customActions.constraints: Must build valid sequence (down in suit on tableau, or next in foundation).

customActions.description: Check whether all 52 cards are on foundations.

engine.deckDescription: One standard 52-card deck consisting of four suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs), each with thirteen ranks from ace down to two. No jokers; used for this patience (solitaire) game with Australian layout and rules.
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs). In Australian Patience, building and tableau rules may alternate by color or suit as specified; all four suits are used in the layout.
engine.rankDescription: Thirteen ranks per suit: ace, king, queen, jack, ten, nine, eight, seven, six, five, four, three, two. Building order (ascending or descending) and foundation rules follow the specific Australian Patience variant.

hero.title: AUSTRALIAN PATIENCE
hero.subtitle: Beyond Klondike
hero.tagline: All cards revealed. No room for error. Can you build the foundations of the outback?

synthesis.shortDescription: A sophisticated 52-card solitaire that challenges you to plan several moves ahead. With all tableau cards visible, the game is no longer about luck, but about precise suit-building and column strategy.

prompts.human: Welcome to Australian Patience! Unlike Klondike, you must build down in the SAME suit. Every card on the table is visible, so take a moment to find your Aces. Remember, once the stock is gone, you're on your own!
prompts.ai: Game: Australian Patience. Type: Solitaire (Scorpion/Klondike mix). Rules: 52 cards. Build down in suit. Any card and its stack can be moved. Stock is 1-by-1, no redeals. Goal: 4 foundations A-K.

scoring.description: Standard solitaire scoring (points per card moved to foundation) or simple win/loss.
scoring.winCondition: Clearing the tableau and stock into the foundations.

nullReasons.cardValues: Australian Patience is usually treated as a simple win or loss without fixed per-card point values.
